overview: The Euwe Attack plays 2.b3 against the Caro-Kann, aiming for a quiet Nimzo-Larsen-style set-up with Bb2 and Nf3. After 2...d5 Black takes the centre (3.Bb2 dxe4 or 3.e5 Bf5) and White gets a slow game with a fianchettoed bishop; theory is minimal. It is an offbeat way to avoid main-line Caro-Kann theory.

white_ideas.idea: Develop Bb2, Nf3 and e3 and aim to take the centre later with c4
Use the long diagonal against the black kingside and the e5 square

black_ideas.idea: Take the centre with ...d5 and ...Nf6, ...Bf5 and ...e6, which is simple and comfortable
Exchange on e4 and play for a Caro-Kann type solid structure

typical_structures.structure: White pawns on b3/e4/d3 against ...c6/d5, a flexible, slow set-up

character.notes: A quiet, low-theory line where neither side takes risks; Black is comfortable. Balanced.

soundness.notes: Sound; a safe if slightly passive alternative.

structure.notes: Centre pawns in tension, undecided: Flexible.

approach.notes: Seldom played by strong players, an offbeat way to dodge theory.

level.notes: Plans are clear and theory is light. Intermediate.

character.reason: Slow flank-style play with no forcing lines.

structure.reason: The centre is undecided with a fianchettoed bishop.

approach.reason: Rare among strong players, though it is a regular surprise.

level.reason: Easy to play but not a standard repertoire choice.

plans.reason: White's bishop on b2 on the long diagonal.
